proposals.evidence: DEDR 2115 gives Tamil/Malayalam kompu, Kannada/Tulu kombu, Telugu/Gadaba kommu, Kota kob and Konda komu ‘horn’. Horn senses select this family; ordinary branch responses are not included in this proposal. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 601 attests Tamil uṇaṅku, Malayalam uṇaṅṅuka, Kannada oṇagu/oṇa/oṇagilu and Kodagu oṇaŋg- dry or wither; Malayalam uṇakku also means dryness. These simple dry stems and ordinary inflections are selected; causative verb phrases and the distinctive Toda forms require separate analysis. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 2408 directly records Tamil caḷi, Kannada caḷi/saḷi, Tulu cali/sali and Telugu calla cold or cool. These simple survey forms are linked to the actual caḷi entry, distinct from taṇ- at 3045; Gondi contact-looking forms are left for donor analysis. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
